We have search results. The first entry seems relevant: reaction_id 1914393 with retro_smarts_template that transforms a C-N bond to a C-Cl bond and a heterocycle? Let's examine: retro_smarts_template: '[#7:7]-[C:6]-[c:5]1:[c:4]:[c:3]:[c:2](-[CH2;D2;+0:1]-[n;H0;D3;+0:12]2:[#7;a:11]:[#7;a:10]:[c:14]:[c:13]:2):[c:9]:[c:8]:1>>Cl-[CH2;D2;+0:1]-[c:2]1:[c:3]:[c:4]:[c:5](-[C:6]-[#7:7]):[c:8]:[c:9]:1.[#7;a:10]1:[#7;a:11]:[nH;D2;+0:12]:[c:13]:[c:14]:1'

So forward reaction (retro template) is product (left side) to precursors (right side). The product is the amine attached to aromatic system; the precursors are a chloromethyl aryl and a heterocycle. This seems like SN2 where nucleophile is amine (attached to carbon) and leaving group is Cl on benzylic position. So applying this template to our target molecule should give two precursors: the chloromethyl aryl (Cl-CH2-aryl) and the heterocycle (maybe a 1,2,4-triazine? Actually the heterocycle is [#7;a:10]1:[#7;a:11]:[nH;D2;+0:12]:[c:13]:[c:14]:1 which is a 1,2,4-triazine? Anyway.

Thus we need to apply this template (ID 1914393) to our molecule. The template ID is reaction_id? The tool expects template_id string. Likely template_id is the reaction_id. So we should use apply_template with template_id "1914393". Let's try.
